
```{r}
library(tidymarkers)
library(knitr)
```

Every figure shows the sequence letters (primers, probe, amplicon), the variant
track, the genomic off-site panel, and on the right the same tumbler as for
KASP. The common principle of this family: discrimination lives **on the
probe** or on single-nucleotide extension, not only at the 3' end of the
primer. Probe placement, its Tm relative to the primers, and the absence of
secondary structure are therefore critical.

## TaqMan

Two allele-specific probes (FAM/HEX) lie between the 3' ends of the primers and
differ by one base. The 5'-exonuclease activity of Taq cleaves the probe only
on a match, releasing the reporter. Rules: the probe must not start with G, the
probe Tm is usually 5–10 °C above the primers, and the variant sits in the
central part of the probe.
[Holland et al. (1991)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.88.16.7276).

```{r taqman-fig, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "TaqMan: a primer pair, two allele-specific probes, the variant in the centre of the probe."}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/taqman.svg")
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
snp <- tibble::tibble(chrom = "Chr1", pos = 300L, ref = "G", alt = "A")
design_taqman_marker(genome, snp, flank = 150)
```

## dPCR

In digital PCR the reaction is partitioned into thousands of droplets; the
number of positive droplets is converted into a concentration by Poisson.
The construct design is the same as for TaqMan (a short amplicon, the probe
between the primers), but the quantitative model requires independent droplets
and minimal competition.
[Hindson et al. (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1021/ac202028g),
[Huggett et al. (2013)](https://doi.org/10.1373/clinchem.2013.206375).

The package designs the construct; partitioning into droplets and the Poisson
conversion are **not simulated** — this is stated explicitly in
`marker_readout()`.

```{r dpcr-fig, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "dPCR: a short amplicon and hydrolysis probes; the droplet model is not simulated."}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/dpcr.svg")
```

## SNaPshot (minisequencing)

One flanking amplicon, then an extension primer whose 3' end abuts the base
before the variant. The polymerase adds one fluorescently labelled ddNTP; the
colour and size of the product tell you which base sits at the variant. The
extension primer must lie inside the amplicon and must not overlap the primers.
[Pastinen et al. (1997)](https://doi.org/10.1101/gr.7.6.606).

```{r snapshot-fig, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "SNaPshot: an amplicon, an extension primer, the 3' end before the variant."}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/snapshot.svg")
```

## castPCR

castPCR is allele-specific TaqMan for a low mutant allele fraction: the ASP
reads the **mutant** base, a WT-specific MGB blocker suppresses the wild type,
and a locus-specific probe registers the product. Key requirements: the ASP is
strictly mutant-specific, the blocker does not interfere with the mutant, and
the probe does not overlap the variant of the ASP. Mechanics of allele-specific
PCR: [Gaudet et al. (2009)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-60327-411-1_26).

```{r castpcr-fig, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "castPCR: a mutant-specific ASP, a WT blocker and a locus-specific probe."}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/castpcr.svg")
```

## What is checked

For all four schemes the common checks are oligo composition, absence of
homodimers/hairpins and Tm/GC. Uniqueness by perfect site is computed for the
TaqMan/dPCR probes and the SNaPshot extension primer; in castPCR it is replaced
by the ASP 3' anchor and the WT blocker. `marker_readout()` notes which part of
the signal is actually modelled.

## Markers that fail: what the package catches and what it does not

A "dud" marker passes the dry design but gives no signal, no discrimination or
no adequate limit of detection in the tube. Below are the concrete failure
mechanisms; for each one it states explicitly what the package **checks**
(gate/acceptance) and what remains a **recommendation** for experimental
validation. A general caveat: thermodynamic checks (hairpins, homodimers,
mismatch dG) are computed only when OligoArrayAux is available; without it the
margin is `NA` and the gate formally passes (`grade_one_marker()`), so a
"green" graph does not by itself prove that the oligos are robust.

### TaqMan

**Checked:** probe composition (GC 40–60%, no 5'-G, no run/SSR), exactly one
perfect site of each probe in the genome, self-structure, Tm window [56, 72] °C,
primer Tm [58, 63] °C, probe mismatch penalty ≥ 1.5 kcal/mol, variant
centrality and amplicon 60–150 bp; with OligoArrayAux the per-allele
discrimination of the probe is additionally computed (`probe_discrimination()`).

- **Probe Tm not 8–10 °C above the primers.** The canonical qPCR rule
  [MacLeod et al. (2021)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7892852/)
  is **not a gate** here: because of the package's compressed Tm scale, the
  ordering "probe hotter than the primers" is only tier2 ranking, and the hard
  window is the absolute [56, 72] °C. A design may pass, but in a real mix the
  probe may lack competition for the template — check on your own
  buffer/instrument.
- **Probe too short or GC-poor.** There is no separate minimum length:
  candidates are enumerated at 18–25 nt, and the extreme GC is filtered out by
  the 40–60% window. This is a candidate filter, not a guarantee of signal; a
  short probe must be tested experimentally.
- **SNP under the probe, but weak discrimination.** The gate requires a
  mismatch dG ≥ 1.5 kcal/mol on the REF probe; this is a thermodynamic proxy,
  not a measured exonuclease discrimination. Without OligoArrayAux the gate
  passes with `NA`. Check with allele dilutions and endpoint fluorescence
  clusters; the mechanics are in
  [Holland et al. (1991)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.88.16.7276).
- **Small allele fraction and WT background.** The endpoint ratio is not
  modelled, nor is the contribution of the wild type or cross-talk between
  dyes. For sub-percent fractions TaqMan is no substitute for dPCR; WT
  controls, NTC and a dilution series are needed.

### dPCR

**Checked:** the same probe composition/specificity/structure, the hard
condition probe Tm ≥ primer Tm + 8 °C, primer Tm [44, 50] °C and an amplicon of
60–150 bp. `probe_discrimination()` computes the on/off efficiency (with
OligoArrayAux), but it does not enter the gates.

- **Probe composition.** Candidates 18–25 nt, GC 40–60%, no 5'-G; as in TaqMan,
  this is a filter, not proof of efficiency.
- **Weak discrimination with the variant under the probe.** Unlike TaqMan,
  there is no separate gate on the mismatch dG — the readout table is
  informational. Allelic discrimination must be confirmed with droplet
  clusters, not only dG.
- **Allele fraction below the limit of detection.** The Poisson conversion and
  the limit of detection are **not simulated** (`marker_readout()`): the
  package does not answer whether the mutant fraction is distinguishable.
  Report per dMIQE
  [Huggett et al. (2013)](https://doi.org/10.1373/clinchem.2013.206375) with a
  confidence interval and a check of the number of positive droplets.
- **Partitioning assumptions.** Droplet independence, equal volume, absence of
  competition/inhibition and threshold correctness are not checked; a review of
  the limitations —
  [Quan et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.3390/s18041271), the platform —
  [Hindson et al. (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1021/ac202028g).
- **WT background.** Only the perfect probe site is taken into account; the
  contribution of WT DNA, false-positive droplets and cross-reactivity are not
  modelled — WT genotypes, NTC and negative droplets are needed.

### SNaPshot

**Checked:** the 3' end of the extension primer exactly one base 5' of the
variant, composition (GC 30–70%, no run/SSR), perfect-site uniqueness,
structure, Tm [50, 55] °C and an amplicon of 100–300 bp.

- **Primer too far or too close.** "Too far" is excluded by construction: the
  candidate must abut the variant. "Close" means exactly adjacent, which is the
  requirement of the method
  [Pastinen et al. (1997)](https://doi.org/10.1101/gr.7.6.606); the placement
  is fixed, so there is no freedom for "too close".
- **Poor 3' design and incomplete extension.** The identity of the 3' base is
  not scored (any base is allowed), and the efficiency of single-nucleotide
  extension, ddNTP incorporation and peak heights are **not simulated**
  (`marker_readout()`). Positive controls and optimisation of the extension
  time are needed; design examples —
  [Fanis et al. (2014)](https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2164-15-108),
  [Namdar Aligoodarzi et al. (2023)](https://doi.org/10.52547/ibj.3856).
- **Dye/mobility.** The channel colour and the mobility of the product in the
  capillary are not modelled; multiplexing and the size standard are verified
  experimentally only.
- **Off-target.** Only the perfect site of the extension primer is checked;
  priming with 1–2 mismatches is not computed.

### castPCR

**Checked:** the ASP 3' base on the variant and its preference for the mutant,
the presence of a WT-specific blocker (3' base = WT), ASP Tm [55, 65] °C, probe
Tm ≥ ASP Tm + 8 °C, amplicon 50–100 bp and blocker composition; the joint
structure of the oligos is computed in `compatibility` but does not enter the
hard gates.

- **ASP and WT blocker balance.** The package picks the longest "clean" WT
  blocker and places the ASP, but does not model their competition or
  concentration ratio. Tune it empirically; mechanism —
  [Barbano et al. (2015)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4686972/),
  [Roma et al. (2013)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3864078/).
- **Blocker does not suppress WT.** Only the WT anchor and the composition are
  checked, while the suppression efficiency and the MGB contribution (the rise
  in effective Tm) are not simulated. WT-only controls and ΔCt are needed; the
  clinical format —
  [Husain et al. (2023)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10334107/).
- **Locus probe.** The placement inside the amplicon without overlap with the
  ASP and Tm > ASP + 8 °C is implemented, but the genomic uniqueness of the
  probe/blocker/ASP is not gated by the designer (unlike TaqMan/dPCR), and MGB
  is not modelled. Check with BLAST/primer-BLAST.
- **Low mutant fraction.** The 0.1–1% limit from the papers is not predicted:
  `marker_readout()` states plainly that ΔCt is not simulated. A dilution
  series of the mutant in WT DNA is needed.

### Off-target and cross-reactivity

In all four schemes uniqueness is computed by **perfect** site
(`max.mismatch = 0`, both orientations); 1–2 mismatches, 3'-seed priming and
probe/blocker cross-reactivity remain outside the check. For diagnostic markers
this is an obligatory external step: primer-BLAST/BLAST, in-silico PCR with
mismatches and negative controls. General rules of qPCR specificity —
[MacLeod et al. (2021)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7892852/).

### Decision audit

`vignettes/figures/decision-{taqman,dpcr,snapshot,castpcr}.{svg,txt}` are the
**scheme** (`plot_decision_tree(scheme = <id>)` without `assay`), not a trace of
a specific candidate: the nodes are neutral, and the block
`assay acceptance checks` only lists the criteria. The SVG figures are a map of
the construct plus a panel of checks; none of them shows endpoint clusters,
droplets, electropherograms or ΔCt. "The graph passed" and "the figure is
green" are therefore different statements.

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/decision-taqman.svg")
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/decision-dpcr.svg")
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/decision-snapshot.svg")
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/decision-castpcr.svg")
```

- **Probe Tm vs primers.** *Visible:* in TaqMan the ordering "probe above the
  primers" stays tier2 (not a gate), in dPCR/castPCR it is a hard +8 °C. SVG:
  TaqMan probes 59.4/61.3 °C with primers at 58.7 (+0.7/+2.6), dPCR —
  57.2/58.1 with 48.8 (+8.4/+9.3), castPCR — 67.7 with ASP 59.0 (+8.7).
  *Weak spot:* `probes$tm[1L]` holds a single Tm for both allelic probes; the
  ALT probe is not recomputed — add its Tm to the gate/tier.

- **Probe placement.** *Visible:* a hard placement node exists only in
  SNaPshot; in TaqMan the placement is set by the soft centrality gate, in dPCR
  there is no node, in castPCR the ASP anchor is hard while the locus probe is a
  candidate filter. *Weak spot:* the graph does not distinguish "adjacent" from
  "with a gap" and does not show which boundary rejected a candidate; on
  failure the designer returns `NULL`. Add a gap node and the reason for
  rejection.

- **Mismatch discrimination.** *Visible:* TaqMan — hard ΔG ≥ 1.5 kcal/mol, but
  for the REF probe only; dPCR — no gate, `probe_discrimination()` stays
  informational (DECIPHER: hybridisation × Taq, not cleavage); SNaPshot —
  discrimination by base, not by ΔG; castPCR — `alt_on − alt_off > 0` (the
  predicted DECIPHER margin), i.e. only the sign. *Weak spot:* the ALT TaqMan
  probe is not scored, in castPCR even 0.001 passes, and the SVG has no
  discrimination/ΔG row; score both alleles with an effect threshold, then
  ΔCt/dilutions.

- **Low allele fraction and WT background.** *Visible:* no DAG has a node for
  "allele fraction", "WT background" or "LOD"; castPCR tier1 is a predicted
  margin, not an LOD. *Weak spot:* LOD and ΔCt are not modelled; do not derive
  the LOD from tier1, set it as an explicit external parameter.

- **Poisson/partitioning.** *Visible:* dPCR has no droplet node; when
  OligoArrayAux is available `marker_readout()` returns `simulated = TRUE` only
  because there is a probe hybridisation table, while
  `readout_assumption("dpcr")` and `scheme$readout` state plainly that
  partitioning/Poisson are not modelled. *Weak spot:* a report must not mix the
  probe table with the Poisson step; copies/µl with CI and the number of
  positive droplets remain external.

- **SNaPshot: extension, ddNTP, dyes.** *Visible:* extension
  placement/composition/uniqueness are hard, while Tm, amplicon and structure
  are **soft** (the ladder can widen them to [45, 60] °C and [50, 350] bp),
  although the first pass lists them as fixed. *Weak spot:* the graph has no
  3'-terminal base, local context, ddNTP efficiency, dye channel or peak
  heights; the SVG is a map, not an electropherogram. Add a 3'-context node and
  do not present soft windows as hard.

- **castPCR: ASP/blocker.** *Visible:* ASP Tm and the amplicon are soft (±2
  °C/±10 bp); the blocker is checked only for presence, 3' base (not mutant)
  and composition, `selection` does not store gate margins, and the figure's
  check panel has no blocker at all
  (`marker_primers.marker_castpcr()` returns the ASP, the primers and the
  probe, but not the blocker). *Weak spot:* no Tm/ΔG, MGB, non-extendable,
  ASP:blocker ratio or suppression efficiency; the blocker should be a separate
  graph node and panel row, not only an entry in `compatibility`.

- **Off-target / cross-reactivity.** *Visible:* exact perfect-site gates exist
  only for the TaqMan/dPCR probes and the SNaPshot extension primer; castPCR has
  none. The `off-target exact primer hits` row in the graph is declarative,
  while the SVG panel computes exact hits for all oligos from
  `marker_primers()` — but for castPCR without the blocker. *Weak spot:* 1–2
  mismatches, the 3'-seed and probe/blocker cross-reactivity are not computed;
  turn this row into an executable gate or remove it from the graph, and keep
  the mismatch-tolerant check external.

A separate point about the evidence of the figure: the Tm panel is scored by
`marker_tm_window()` (58–62 °C for dPCR primers, 65–72 °C for probes), not by
the gates (dPCR primers 44–50 °C; TaqMan probe 56–72 °C). Hence the red rows
in the SVG: dPCR primers at 48.8 °C and probes at 57.2/58.1 °C get `broken`
even though the gates let them through; in TaqMan the probes at 59.4/61.3 °C
are also `broken` although the gate is [56, 72]. Fix the mapping table or label
the colour as a heuristic.

A correction to the first pass: the soft windows are TaqMan
centrality/amplicon/structure, dPCR amplicon/structure, SNaPshot
amplicon/Tm/structure, castPCR amplicon/ASP Tm; the ladder shifts them, so these
are ideal thresholds, not hard boundaries. References for the mechanisms are
the same as above (Holland 1991; Pastinen 1997; Hindson 2011; Huggett 2013;
Barbano 2015; Roma 2013; MacLeod 2021).
